patterns.name: AI is now solving research-level maths problems
patterns.line: Anthropic and OpenAI each posted a proof of VP versus VNP, a stepping stone to P versus NP, on the same day. It follows AI results on Navier-Stokes in September and the Riemann hypothesis last week.
patterns.why: Maths has proof checkers, so AI results can be verified. Theoretical computer scientists lose ground to machines that finish decades of work in days.
patterns.watch: Whether human mathematicians confirm either proof and whether it carries over to P versus NP.

patterns.name: AI trade is hitting both stocks and AI startup valuations
patterns.line: Anthropic fell to about $76, below its $83 IPO price, less than a week after debuting at $111.50. Nvidia fell over 7% midday, giving back part of Monday's 30%-plus jump.
patterns.why: Public prices now set the benchmark for private AI valuations. A weak Anthropic can squeeze startup rounds and IPO plans.
patterns.watch: Whether Anthropic holds above its $83 IPO price this week.

takeaways.line: Amazon is buying software, not chips, to narrow Nvidia's lead. If Decart's stack lets models switch chips easily, Nvidia's CUDA lock-in weakens, and rivals like Anthropic could gain cheaper compute.
A second US Section 301 finding could stack on the 10% duty already imposed on India in July. That would shrink the tariff edge India was promised in trade talks.
Congo's cobalt halt props up prices and rewards producers like CMOC. It also pushes Chinese buyers toward recycling and Indonesian supply, which can erode Congo's leverage over time.
With no cover deal at COP31, climate action shifts to voluntary coalitions such as the roughly 80-nation electrification target. Progress then depends on willing countries, not consensus.

money.line: Data security startup raised a round led by Tanglin Venture Partners, with IIFL Fintech Fund, Kalaari Capital and Endiya Partners among investors.
Bengaluru startup making robot actuators raised from Avaana Capital (lead), WEH Ventures and angels to build a factory.

lead.headline: Anthropic and OpenAI both claim proofs on a key step toward P versus NP
lead.hook: Anthropic and OpenAI each published a proof of VP versus VNP on the same day, with Anthropic's upload about 6 hours earlier, according to timestamps.
points: VP versus VNP is a stepping stone to P versus NP, one of seven Millennium Prize problems with a $1 million award. It replaces binary logic with arithmetic, which gives a more structured problem.

Anthropic says an internal research version of Claude proved VNP is not contained in VP, and also wrote the paper and a formalisation (the proof as checkable computer code). It says no human mathematician has checked it.
OpenAI's paper, also with a formalisation, is similar in places but differs on key points.
Two other Millennium problems have fallen to AI: Navier-Stokes in September and the Riemann hypothesis last week. The Poincaré conjecture fell in 2010.

Cambridge's Tom Gur calls it 'decades of progress in days' but says the community needs time to see how general the technique is. Oxford's Varun Kanade expects new techniques will still be needed for P versus NP.
lead.evidence_of: AI is now solving research-level maths problems

frontpage.headline: US weighs new tariffs on India, China and 14 other economies
frontpage.hook: The US may raise tariffs on India, China and others after a Section 301 probe into 16 economies' industrial subsidies, with results possible as early as this week.
points: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer could announce findings soon, with China likely facing some of the highest tariffs, per the Wall Street Journal.
The probe, launched in March, covers excess capacity and subsidies that let foreign firms undercut US makers. It includes the EU, Japan, South Korea, Mexico and India.
In July the USTR imposed an extra 10% duty on Indian imports under the same law.
An Indian official says the US promised India a tariff edge over rivals in the trade deal, but it depends on the final structure. India wants the first tranche done by the end of the financial year.

frontpage.headline: Anthropic shares drop below IPO price
frontpage.hook: Anthropic stock fell to as low as $76 on Tuesday, below its $83 IPO price and nearly 12% under Monday's close, less than a week after it debuted at $111.50.
points: Trading below the IPO price is read as negative, since offerings are usually priced at a discount to expected value.
VCs watch Anthropic as a barometer of how public markets value AI.
Continued weakness could pressure private startup valuations and weaken IPO prospects for other AI firms.
Nvidia also fell over 7% by midday, giving back part of Monday's 30%-plus gain after Jensen Huang's reinstatement as CEO.
frontpage.evidence_of: AI trade is hitting both stocks and AI startup valuations

frontpage.headline: Food prices are driving India's inflation back up
frontpage.hook: India's retail inflation rose to 6.09% in October from 5.54% in September, with food inflation at 8.94%.
points: Rural food inflation was 9.09% against 8.68% urban. The poorest rural fifth faced 6.9% inflation versus 6.5% for the richest fifth.
Causes: a monsoon 13% below normal, El Niño, supply shortages and higher input costs. Food is 36.75% of the CPI basket, down from 45.86%.
Crisil says a vegetarian thali cost 12% more year on year. Rice rose about 10%, pulses 8%, edible oil 13% and LPG 10%, and the rise is broadening.
Government cereal stocks are well above minimums and a free-food scheme covers nearly 800 million people. Economists warn of a wage-price spiral if wages chase prices.

frontpage.headline: DR Congo suspends cobalt exports from November 30
frontpage.hook: Congo, which holds 6 million tonnes of cobalt reserves, 37.5 times China's, will suspend all cobalt exports from November 30 until further notice.
points: Regulator Arecoms says the halt targets a 'persistent imbalance' of weak demand, rising inventories and excess supply. It covers industrial and artisanal output and will be reviewed after four months.
Cobalt metal was $18.15 per pound, 24% lower than at the start of 2026. Weak consumer-electronics sales, hit by memory-chip-driven phone price rises, are cited.
CMOC, the top producer, is rushing cargoes out this week. Huayou says its quota of just over 1,000 tonnes and Indonesian mines limit its exposure.
The last halt since February 2025 ran over seven months and prices rose. Analysts expect higher prices again, and more recycling and non-Congo supply.

frontpage.headline: COP31 ends without a cover deal, longest summit on record
frontpage.hook: COP31 in Antalya ran nearly 50 hours over time, the longest ever, and ended with its 'Antalya pact' rejected by the EU, UK and climate-vulnerable states.
points: The pact dropped mentions of fossil fuels and lacked concrete adaptation finance figures; at least 32 countries rejected it.
Other items passed, including just transition, climate finance work programme, and a global goal on adaptation.
Agriculture talks collapsed for the second year in a row after disputes over the EU's carbon border tax and agroecology, and resume next year.
About 80 nations signed a target of 35% of final energy from electricity by 2035. Next year's COP is in Addis Ababa.

frontpage.headline: India's informal businesses grow at record pace, but hiring lags
frontpage.hook: India's informal (unincorporated) establishments rose 18.81% year on year to 9.47 crore in July-September, while employment grew 16.86% to 15.03 crore, both series highs.
points: Hired workers grew only about 5% to 3.49 crore. Working owners are about 62% of workers, up from 59.98%.
Workers per establishment fell to 1.59 from 1.61, so firms are more numerous, not bigger.
Services led: 'other services' employment rose over 33%. Manufacturing establishments grew 10.55% but employment just 3.52%.
Registered establishments rose to 43.28% from 37.20%. The survey excludes construction and is not a measure of GDP or overall jobs.

frontpage.headline: DRDO hires Pune startup for jam-proof laser links to drones
frontpage.hook: DRDO awarded olee.space, founded in 2023, a contract (value undisclosed) to build laser communication terminals for drones within 18 months.
points: Radio jamming in the Russia-Ukraine war pushed drones onto fibre-optic cables, which limit range and can snag.
Laser links send data on a narrow light beam through open air, giving fibre-like speed, with no radio jamming vulnerability, and are hard to intercept.
The system has a tripod ground terminal and a drone payload with automatic pointing and tracking for a two-way link.
olee.space raised $3 million seed in August 2025 led by Rockstud Capital.

frontpage.headline: Amazon buys Decart's chip-optimisation tech for a reported $7.5B
frontpage.hook: Amazon will acquire Decart's technology and team for a reported $7.5 billion to make its Trainium AI chips run models better against Nvidia.
points: Decart's software, the Decart Optimization Stack, helps AI models run efficiently across chips from Nvidia, Amazon and Google. Amazon has worked with it since 2025; Amazon did not disclose terms.
Nvidia's CUDA software makes switching costly for customers; Decart is meant to ease that.
Nvidia invested in Decart's $300 million round at a $4 billion valuation. Anthropic reportedly also tried to buy it.
Anthropic already uses Trainium, with nearly one million Trainium2 chips on Project Rainier. AWS and Nvidia also plan two million more Nvidia GPUs on AWS.

stories.headline: Tidal bans fully AI-generated music
stories.hook: Tidal will remove all tracks it judges 100% AI-generated from December 9; 27 million such songs make up 6.3% of its catalogue.
points: In 90 days, 43% of distributed tracks were fully AI, and on 6 November 60% of uploads were.
96% of those tracks got zero streams in three months. Tidal removed 65,000 suspected artist impersonations.
AI-assisted tracks stay; fully AI tracks are caught via metadata. Tidal says they divert royalties from artists.
Bandcamp banned AI music in January. Spotify and Apple Music label it but allow it; Spotify deleted 75 million 'spammy' tracks.

stories.headline: Novartis CEO: AI will cut drug development by four years, not cure all disease
stories.hook: Novartis CEO Vas Narasimhan expects AI to cut average drug development from 12 years to eight within a decade, far short of curing cancer in five to 10.
points: He cites limited understanding of human biology, so long animal and human trials stay. Up to two of the four years come from the pre-trial stage.
He expects clinical success rates to rise from 8% to 12%.
This contrasts with Anthropic's Dario Amodei and Demis Hassabis, who suggested diseases could be cured within a decade.
Anthropic is buying Coefficient Bio. Isomorphic raised $5 billion last week and works with Novartis.

also.line: Physical AI startup Provision Labs is acquiring home-services platform Pronto, per Moneycontrol, to use real-world data to train physical AI; Pronto's investors become Provision shareholders.

stories.headline: First industry-built PSLV to launch in Q1 2027
stories.hook: India's first PSLV made fully by industry is due to launch in Q1 2027, ISRO chief V. Narayanan said, under an ₹860 crore contract for five rockets.
points: A HAL-L&T consortium builds the five rockets under a contract from NSIL, ISRO's commercial arm. Earlier, ISRO built PSLV with industry support.
India has 56 space assets and needs many more communication and earth-observation satellites, which he says the government cannot do alone.
The Gaganyaan orbital module is in its final stages; the first uncrewed flight is to carry an AI-enabled half-humanoid robot.

stories.headline: Draft rules would require batteries with larger rooftop solar
stories.hook: India's draft rules would make rooftop solar consumers install storage of at least 20% of daily generation, from April 1, 2028.
points: States set the size threshold; if they do not, it applies above 10 kW.
The aim is to shift surplus daytime solar to evening peaks, easing discoms' costs of managing swings and buying expensive peak power.
States may also levy net-metering charges above a threshold, citing fixed-cost recovery and cross-subsidy by other consumers.
Time-of-day tariffs are deferred to April 2028 (above 10 kW) and April 2029 for other non-agricultural consumers.

stories.headline: India's solar installations set for a record year
stories.hook: The IEA expects India to beat 2025's record 38 GW of solar additions in 2026, after installing 32 GW in January-August.
points: Capacity tripled from 2020 to about 140 GW. Developers are rushing before domestic solar cell sourcing rules fully apply.
The IEA expects a short slowdown afterwards, because auction volumes in 2025 and 2026 are lower.
By 2030 capacity should exceed 350 GW, 2.5 times today's.
In 2025 average solar auction tariffs were about 40% below the cost of coal power.

also.line: Amazon plans to invest $7 billion in Indian renewable energy projects by 2030, on top of $4 billion already contracted there.

stories.headline: India weighs letting foreign drugmakers run early-stage trials locally
stories.hook: India's drug regulator has begun informal consultations on loosening norms that now limit early-phase clinical studies in India.
points: The government is preparing regulatory changes to attract global pharma research.
One proposal would let multinational drugmakers run early-stage trials in India.
Officials describe the consultations as informal; no timeline or details are given.

stories.headline: WFP chief warns trade-route disruption raises food aid costs
stories.hook: WFP head Luke Lindberg told the UN Security Council that disruptions on three major trade routes are pushing up food and relief costs (headline says 7.3 million more people's aid is at risk).
points: He spoke on Monday, November 23.
Higher costs hit when millions can least bear them.
Only a brief excerpt was available, so no further figures are given (summary from limited source text).

stories.headline: Sarvam launches voice dictation API for English and 22 Indian languages
stories.hook: Sarvam's Dictate API costs ₹0.50 per minute of audio and combines speech recognition and transcript editing in one call.
points: It pairs the Saaras V4 speech model with a Sarvam 105B language model trained to edit. It handles mid-sentence switches between languages and self-corrections.
Sarvam claims 40% fewer character edits than Google's Gemini 3.5 Transcribe on English clips up to a minute, and 47% fewer across Indian languages and Hinglish.
Developers can add up to 1,000 names or terms per request. It supports live dictation and recordings up to an hour.
Its dictation app Kivi has logged over 30 million dictated words. Sarvam says Token Factory runs on privately procured GPUs, answering questions on subsidised compute.
Nasscom projects India's voice AI market at $1.8 billion by 2030.

stories.headline: IG Defence test-fires JWALA MK-1 counter-drone micro-missile
stories.hook: Noida's IG Defence test-fired JWALA MK-1, a 5 km-range counter-drone micro-missile it calls India's first self-operating, at Pokhran on Monday.
points: It runs on GRID, the company's AI mission-autonomy system, which detects, identifies and classifies targets and manages engagement.
The firm argues costly interceptors against cheap drones strain inventories and economics, so affordable, mass-producible defences are needed.
It aims to reduce dependence on foreign defence technology.

stories.headline: Navy and Coast Guard plan 76 utility helicopters
stories.hook: The Indian Navy (51) and Coast Guard (25) plan to buy 76 utility helicopters worth about ₹15,000 crore to replace ageing Cheetah/Chetak choppers.
points: Indian firms would partner with foreign makers to build them in India, under the Buy and Make (Indian) category; a Defence Ministry meeting is expected soon.
The Army and Air Force want 400 light helicopters, 200 from HAL and 200 from private firms; that private programme is cleared and a tender is due.
The Navy earlier planned 111 such helicopters but that project stalled; it also plans 60 UH Marine from HAL.

stories.headline: US blacklists Megaspeed over alleged Nvidia chip diversion
stories.hook: The US put Singapore's Megaspeed International and six affiliates in Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand on its Entity List on Monday.
points: Anyone supplying them with advanced US technology, including Nvidia GPUs, now needs a US export licence.
The US is investigating alleged diversion of Nvidia chips to China. Megaspeed denies wrongdoing; Singapore is also examining it.
US officials accuse former Megaspeed executive Alice Huang of working with China's Ministry of State Security against Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang; Beijing rejects this.
Trump said Huang's return poses no national security risk and urged Nvidia to continue its export-compliance probe.

stories.headline: Pixxel plans 2.5 lakh sq ft satellite factory near Bengaluru airport
stories.hook: Pixxel's GigaPixxel plant is planned to build 50 satellites in parallel by mid-2027, 100 by end-2027 and 200 by mid-2028.
points: It will make hyperspectral Earth-observation satellites and open in 2027, near Kempegowda airport.
Karnataka won out against Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu after Pixxel's CTO flagged difficulties getting land.
Pixxel has six Firefly satellites in orbit, reported NASA and US NRO contracts, and leads a consortium for India's first private national 12-satellite constellation.

also.line: Bank of Korea is expected to resume rate hikes this week as a chip boom drives stronger growth and keeps inflation elevated, per Bloomberg Economics, despite weak domestic demand.

stories.headline: Two Indians among 11 hurt in Houthi attack on Riyadh tower
stories.hook: Eleven people, including two Indians, were injured when Houthis hit a tower in Riyadh's financial district on Tuesday, Saudi authorities said.
points: The injured: two Saudis, two Indians, three Nepalese and four Egyptians. The Indian embassy is assisting.
It is the second attack on the district in under a week; Thursday's strike damaged several floors of a tower.
The PIF tower, headquarters of Saudi Arabia's sovereign wealth fund, was reportedly among those hit.
Houthi authorities allege Saudi-led strikes in Al-Hudaydah on Monday killed 17 workers.

stories.headline: FSSAI sanctions prosecution of Bisleri over a water sample
stories.hook: FSSAI sanctioned prosecution of Bisleri on November 22 after a sample was declared unsafe, though Bisleri says its water is safe.
points: A sample failed on bromate (12 micrograms per litre vs a 10 limit). A referral lab then declared it unsafe for polynuclear aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs).

Bisleri says the sample came from its Goa plant, one of 143. It says the referral lab found bromate within limits and an independent lab agreed, and it thought the matter was closed after sending results on February 2, 2026.
Parliament data showed 333 of 1,300 packaged-water samples failed in 2023-24.

stories.headline: China-linked network uses AI fakes against Taiwan's ruling party
stories.hook: BBC Verify found a China-linked network posted over 500 fake videos about Taiwan's DPP in a year, viewed tens of millions of times, more than half in the last four months.
points: Fakes claim President Lai Ching-te holds a US green card and would abandon Taiwan, which his office denies. Deepfakes show Taipei mayoral candidate Puma Shen using drugs, which he denies.
Accounts linked to Chinese firm Borderless and posting in office hours point to a professional operation.
Taiwan flagged nearly 2,700 accounts to Meta, which removed them.
Experts say the aim is to erode trust and deepen polarisation ahead of local elections.

stories.headline: Huang's return to Nvidia is a mixed blessing for China
stories.hook: Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO after Trump's intervention looks good for Beijing, but his hands may be tied.
points: Huang is the leading US advocate for selling advanced chips to China; several Chinese tech executives welcomed his return.
Washington lawmakers are lining up to question him and tighten chip-sale rules.
Either way, it gives Beijing more reason to wean companies off US technology (summary from limited source text).

also.line: Israel's Eisenkot (21 seats) signed a first coalition pact with Lieberman (7); he has until December 6 to form a government, against Likud's 53 of 120 seats.

stories.headline: AI models find a shared brain code across 21 languages
stories.hook: An MIT study found the brain processes 21 languages in a shared way, using AI models to predict brain responses.
points: Encoding models built from multilingual AI models and brain scans predicted responses in all 21 languages, even Marathi and Lithuanian with limited data.
A model trained on French predicted Vietnamese brain activity without having seen it, suggesting a shared representation, apparently tied to meaning.
This could extend brain-disorder diagnostic tools beyond English and help with dying languages.

stories.headline: mRNA nose drops restore memory in old mice
stories.hook: University of Sydney researchers say mRNA nose drops returned old mice's memory performance to youthful levels and stopped decline in Alzheimer's-model mice.
points: The drops deliver mRNA that makes BDNF, a protein supporting neurons, bypassing the blood-brain barrier.
Treated Alzheimer's-model mice, dosed twice weekly from two months old, showed no further decline by four months, without plaques falling.
It is so far tested only in mice; animal safety studies come first, and the team hopes for human trials within two years.

stories.headline: Psilocybin and ketamine reduce habit-driven choices in mice
stories.hook: Both psilocybin and ketamine made mice make fewer errors, relying on current cues rather than repeated habits, in a Boston University study.
points: Mice made more accurate choices but took longer to decide: a speed-accuracy trade-off.
Recordings in the orbitofrontal cortex show core activity patterns preserved, with subtle widespread shifts.
The team aims to find the pathways involved, to build therapies without hallucinogenic effects.

also.line: Economist William Nordhaus, who brought climate change into economic analysis and won the 2018 Nobel Prize in Economics, has died, Nature reports (summary from limited source text).

stories.headline: 72% of India's tech workers would switch careers, survey finds
stories.hook: Blind's survey of 2,958 India-based professionals found 72% would change to a completely different career if cost and retraining were free.
points: 30% would switch immediately and 42% if pay stayed the same; only 13% are happy.
56% would not encourage their children into tech; only 4% would recommend software engineering, versus 34% healthcare and 19% AI and machine learning.
Blind posts about leaving software engineering are up 37.5% on all of 2025. The survey does not show AI caused the sentiment.

also.line: Google Cloud India denied mass layoffs but confirmed about 30 roles cut last week in a reprioritisation, after unverified Blind posts claimed wider cuts.

stories.headline: Pakistan's first astronaut flies on China's Shenzhou 24
stories.hook: Pakistani air force pilot Muhammad Zeeshan Ali became the first foreign national to board China's Tiangong space station after Shenzhou 24 docked.
points: He joins Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi and will stay about a week, studying photosynthesis in bacteria and radiation effects on quinoa seeds.
Pakistan has no crewed spacecraft; only the US, China and Russia have flown people on homegrown craft.
China aims to put astronauts on the Moon by 2030 and offers a route to space for other countries.

also.line: Gukesh drew the World Championship opening game against Uzbekistan's Javokhir Sindarov after escaping a prepared line (summary from limited source text).

opportunities.name: AIM Safety Fellowship 2027
opportunities.summary: Three-month AI safety research fellowship from February 1, 2027 with weekly mentoring; Seoul-based, remote possible. Stipend not stated.

opportunities.name: Better Futures Fellowship 2027
opportunities.summary: Nine-week online programme with a five-week course and a four-week public project; assumes prior EA or AI-safety familiarity.

opportunities.name: Primewise Founders Club Networking Event
opportunities.summary: Online founder-investor networking for 25-40 people; a confirmation form is required before registering.
